seoTitle: Connect Namecheap Domain to Blogger & Fix 404 Error
metaDescription: Connect a Namecheap domain to Blogger with the exact CNAME and A records Google requires, and fix the 404 error that shows up when a record is missing.
intro: Connecting a Namecheap domain to a Blogger blog gives your site a branded web address, but it commonly throws a 404 error if the DNS records aren't set up exactly right. Blogger's Custom domain field and Namecheap's Advanced DNS records have to agree with each other precisely, and a single missing or extra record is usually the whole story behind the error. This guide walks through both panels, plus the record that most guides skip: the one that makes the bare domain (without www) work at all.
prerequisites: A Blogger blog you already own, currently on its default blogspot.com address

steps.heading: Set your custom domain in Blogger
steps.body: In Blogger, open Settings, find Publishing, and click Custom domain. Type the domain you want to use with the www prefix, for example www.yourdomain.com, since Blogger's setup is built around the www subdomain by default. Hit Save. Blogger will immediately try to verify the domain and fail, because Namecheap doesn't have the matching DNS records yet. That's expected; this step just tells Blogger what to look for, and its error message is where the exact CNAME values you need come from.

image.caption: Blogger's Custom domain dialog under Settings → Publishing, with a www subdomain entered before the matching DNS records exist.

steps.heading: Log in to Namecheap and open Advanced DNS
steps.body: Sign in to Namecheap, go to Domain List, find the domain you just entered into Blogger, and click Manage. Open the Advanced DNS tab; this is where every record below gets added.

image.caption: The Namecheap dashboard's Domain List, showing an active domain and its Manage button.

steps.heading: Add the CNAME records Blogger requires
steps.body: Use Add New Record for two CNAME entries: one with host www pointing to ghs.google.com, and a second, longer verification CNAME with a unique host and value that Blogger generated specifically for your domain in the previous step. Set the type to CNAME, copy the host and value exactly, leave TTL on Automatic, and click the checkmark to save each one, then Save All Changes.

image.caption: Namecheap's Advanced DNS panel with a CNAME record mapping the www host to ghs.google.com, alongside an existing TXT record.

steps.heading: Add four A records if you want the bare domain to work
steps.body: The www CNAME alone only makes www.yourdomain.com load. If you also want yourdomain.com, without the www, to reach your blog, Google's own domain-setup documentation requires four A records on the root host (@), pointing at Google's IP addresses (see the table below for the exact values). Add all four, then in Blogger's Publishing settings turn on Redirect domain so visitors who land on the bare domain get forwarded to the www version. Skip this step entirely if you're fine with only the www address working; the CNAME from the previous step is enough on its own.

steps.heading: Remove conflicting records
steps.body: A 404 error after adding the right records is very often caused by leftover records that conflict with them, most commonly an old A record, URL redirect record, or parking-page CNAME still pointed at Namecheap's default hosting on the www or root host. DNS only resolves one way for a given host, so if Namecheap is still serving its own placeholder for www while a CNAME also points www at Google, the result is inconsistent or wrong. Scan the Advanced DNS list for anything else touching www or @, and delete it.

steps.heading: Wait for propagation, then verify both versions
steps.body: DNS changes don't apply instantly. Namecheap's own guidance is roughly 30 minutes for new records to take effect, though full propagation across the internet's resolvers can take longer. Once you've given it some time, go back to Blogger's Custom domain field and save it again to trigger a fresh verification, or just load the site. If www.yourdomain.com still 404s, check the CNAME values character by character; a single wrong character in the verification record is the most common reason this drags on. If the bare yourdomain.com doesn't load while www does, that almost always means the four A records from the previous step are missing, not that anything is wrong with the www setup.

troubleshooting.problem: www.yourdomain.com shows a 404 after saving in Blogger
troubleshooting.cause: An old A record, redirect record, or parking CNAME on the www host is still conflicting with the new CNAME pointing to ghs.google.com.
troubleshooting.fix: Open Advanced DNS and delete anything else touching the www host, keeping only the CNAME to ghs.google.com.

troubleshooting.problem: The bare domain (yourdomain.com, without www) doesn't load, but www works fine
troubleshooting.cause: The four A records for the root host were never added; Blogger's Redirect domain toggle has nothing to redirect from without them.
troubleshooting.fix: Add the four A records listed in the table above, pointing @ at Google's IPs, then enable Redirect domain in Blogger's Publishing settings.

troubleshooting.problem: Blogger still won't verify after adding the right-looking records
troubleshooting.cause: A single mistyped character in the long verification CNAME's host or value, or not enough time has passed for propagation.
troubleshooting.fix: Recheck the verification CNAME against Blogger's exact error message character by character, then wait and retry; Namecheap's own records typically take about 30 minutes to activate.

faq.question: Why do I get a 404 error after connecting my domain to Blogger?
faq.answer: Usually a mismatched or conflicting CNAME record in Namecheap's Advanced DNS. Leftover A records or parking-page CNAMEs on the same host as your new records are the most common cause.

faq.question: Do I need to change nameservers to connect to Blogger?
faq.answer: No. Adding specific CNAME and A records in Namecheap's Advanced DNS panel is enough; you don't need to change nameservers.

faq.question: How long until my custom domain works on Blogger?
faq.answer: Namecheap's own records typically activate in around 30 minutes, though full DNS propagation can occasionally take longer.

faq.question: Do I need the four A records, or just the www CNAME?
faq.answer: Just the www CNAME if you only care about www.yourdomain.com working. The four A records are only needed if you also want the bare domain, without www, to resolve.

faq.question: Can I use a subdomain instead of the root domain for Blogger?
faq.answer: Yes. Blogger supports connecting a subdomain, which sidesteps the root-domain A records and redirect setup entirely.
